title: Microsoft Teams: manage Microsoft 365 certified apps through org-wide third-party app settings
summary: The documented controls, licensing basis and administrator-action default are supported. The briefing correctly distinguishes the completed rollout in Microsoft's notice from the roadmap's Rolling out status. Two minor qualifications are needed: the anonymous-meeting licensing exception and the scope of the 60-day notice promise.

claims.quote: Microsoft Teams: Streamlined Microsoft 365 Certified App Management in Teams Admin Center

claims.quote: "releasePhase": ["General Availability"]

claims.where: What's changing: first paragraph; title; summary
claims.claim: The roadmap says administrators can enable Microsoft 365 certified SaaS applications through org-wide third-party app settings.
claims.quote: This feature allows Microsoft 365 administrators to enable Microsoft 365 certified SaaS applications within their tenant through org-wide settings for third-party apps.

claims.where: What's changing: first paragraph; Open questions
claims.claim: The roadmap says admins can allow a subset of applications verified against industry security and compliance standards.
claims.quote: Admins can choose to allow a subset of applications that have already been verified against industry security and compliance standards.

claims.claim: The roadmap describes reducing approval overhead while maintaining governance.
claims.quote: This ensures organizations can confidently adopt apps while maintaining governance and reducing approval overhead.

claims.where: What's changing: second paragraph; Scope; changes; Open questions
claims.claim: MC796790 places certified SaaS app management in Phase 2 and says it has completely rolled out to all tenants.
claims.quote: As part of this phase we will also enable administrators to manage Microsoft 365 certified SaaS applications within their tenant through org-wide settings for third-party apps. This has been rolled out completely for all tenants.

claims.where: front matter: defaultState; summary; Why it matters; rationale: risk and impact
claims.claim: The default is admin-opt-in: Phase 2 changes neither org-wide nor app-level settings without administrator action.
claims.quote: Note: In this phase, no changes will be applied to org-wide settings or app-level settings without administrator action.

claims.claim: The bulk control is in Teams admin center > Teams apps > Manage apps > Actions > Org-wide app settings > Third-party apps.
claims.quote: Sign in to the Teams admin center and access Teams apps > Manage apps. ... On Manage apps page, under the Actions menu, select Org-wide app settings. ... Under Third-party apps, a single control manages the bulk availability of both the new and existing third-party agents and apps.

claims.claim: No PowerShell or Microsoft Graph setting for the org-wide Third-party apps control is documented at the time of writing.
claims.quote: Searched: Teams org-wide Third-party apps control PowerShell MicrosoftTeams Graph teamsAppSettings; Graph beta teamsAppSettings third party apps. Read manage-apps, app-centric-management, teamsAppSettings v1.0/beta and Graph cmdlet excerpts.

claims.where: controls[1].ui; Governance controls: second row; Governance guidance
claims.claim: A specific app can be allowed or blocked in Teams admin center > Teams apps > Manage apps > app > Allow or Block.
claims.quote: Sign in to the Teams admin center and access Teams apps > Manage apps. Select the app on the Manage apps page and select Allow or Block option.

claims.claim: MicrosoftTeams PowerShell supports Update-M365TeamsApp -Id <app id> -IsBlocked <Boolean> to change an app's tenant state.
claims.quote: Module: MicrosoftTeams PowerShell module. This cmdlet updates app state and app available values for the Microsoft Teams app. -Id: Application ID of Microsoft Teams app. -IsBlocked: The state of the app in the tenant. Type: Boolean.

claims.claim: The cmdlet reference describes an example using -IsBlocked $true as unblocking the app.
claims.quote:
Update-M365TeamsApp -Id 4c4ec2e8-4a2c-4bce-8d8f-00fc664a4e5b -IsBlocked $true
Unblocks Bookings app (App ID 4c4ec2e8-4a2c-4bce-8d8f-00fc664a4e5b).

claims.where: controls[0].governs and note; What's changing; Governance controls
claims.claim: Learn describes a single Third-party apps control for bulk availability of new and existing third-party apps.
claims.quote: Under Third-party apps, a single control manages the bulk availability of both the new and existing third-party agents and apps.

claims.where: Why it matters; Risk assessment: Data exposure
claims.claim: Org-wide app settings govern the default availability of new apps.
claims.quote: The Org-wide app settings apply to: All the new apps made available in Teams app store.

claims.where: Why it matters; Risk assessment: Data exposure
claims.claim: Org-wide app settings govern existing apps whose availability administrators have not individually changed.
claims.quote: The Org-wide app settings apply to: All the existing apps that you didn't actively manage, that is, you didn't change the availability of.

claims.where: Why it matters; Risk assessment: Data exposure; Governance guidance
claims.claim: The bulk Third-party apps control is not restricted to Microsoft 365 certified apps.
claims.quote: After migrating to app-centric management, a single control now manages bulk availability for both new and existing third-party apps. Toggle on to enable all new and existing third-party apps across the tenant; toggle off to disable all. App-level settings stay intact.

claims.where: Why it matters; Risk assessment: Data exposure; Governance controls
claims.claim: Individually saved app availability assignments are exempt from org-wide defaults.
claims.quote: The Org-wide app settings don't apply to: All apps that have user assignment set to Specific users and groups and saved by you. All apps that were assigned to Everyone or to No one and saved individually.

claims.where: Why it matters; Risk assessment: Data exposure; Governance controls
claims.claim: Blocked apps are exempt from org-wide app settings.
claims.quote: The Org-wide app settings don't apply to: ... Any blocked apps.

claims.where: controls[0].note; Risk assessment: Change & support; Governance controls
claims.claim: The post-migration Third-party apps control does not override app-level configurations.
claims.quote: Post app centric management migration, these are unified into a single control that governs bulk availability for both new and existing third-party apps. ... This control doesn't override app-level configurations.

claims.where: summary; What's changing; Why it matters; Cost and licensing
claims.claim: The Apps to consider allowing tile counts Microsoft 365 certified apps.
claims.quote: The Teams admin center now includes Apps to consider allowing tile on the Manage apps page. This tile displays counts of Microsoft 365 certified and publisher-attested agents and apps

claims.claim: The Apps to consider allowing tile also counts publisher-attested apps.
claims.quote: This tile displays counts of Microsoft 365 certified and publisher-attested agents and apps, helping admins quickly identify trusted agents and apps.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Data exposure
claims.claim: An app's details page has a Security and Compliance tab for its certification and security information.
claims.quote: A new Security and Compliance tab on each app's details page displays its certification status, publisher attestation, and key security attributes

claims.where: What's changing; Why it matters; Open questions
claims.claim: Learn documents no certified-only option within the org-wide Third-party apps control at the time of writing.
claims.quote: Searched: Teams admin center Third-party apps certified-only option allow only Microsoft 365 certified SaaS apps org-wide settings. Read manage-apps, app-centric-management and overview-of-app-certification; found filtering and per-app management, not a certified-only bulk switch.

claims.claim: Certification incorporates information attested by the vendor.
claims.quote: Developers provide answers to a questionnaire as part of their Teams app's security and compliance information for Publisher Attestation and for Microsoft 365 certification.

claims.claim: The certification program audits apps against industry-standard frameworks.
claims.quote: Microsoft 365 app compliance program checks and audits an app against controls that are derived from leading industry-standard frameworks.

claims.claim: An app's page in Teams admin center links to its privacy policy.
claims.quote: In Teams admin center, each app page links to the privacy statement and terms of use of the app.

claims.claim: Consent to required permissions is separate from allowing an app.
claims.quote: Once you decide to approve the use of an app, ensure that the app adoption is smooth for the users. A crucial part of the process is granting consent to the permissions that an app needs to work.

claims.claim: Only a Global admin can give the final consent and apply changes for the documented tenant-unification cases.
claims.quote: Only a Global admin can give consent and apply the final changes.

claims.claim: Teams or Global admins can prepare tenant-unification updates through the Review summary page.
claims.quote: Any Teams or Global admin can make updates upto the Review summary page.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Change & support; Governance guidance: At rollout
claims.claim: Saved org-wide app settings take effect after a few hours.
claims.quote: Select Save. The settings take effect after a few hours.

claims.claim: In unified tenants, changes in Teams admin center and Microsoft 365 admin center synchronize between the portals.
claims.quote: After your tenant is unified, all changes to org-wide settings, agent app, status, or availability in TAC are automatically synchronized in MAC and vice versa.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing; rationale: cost
claims.claim: Each user needs a Teams licence before using Teams.
claims.quote: Except for joining Teams meetings anonymously, each user in your organization must have a Teams license before they can use Teams.
claims.fix: Qualify the licensing sentence and repeated notes as: 'Except for joining Teams meetings anonymously, each user in your organization needs a Teams licence before using Teams.' The exception does not change the licence needed to use the apps discussed here.

claims.claim: The licensing model is included under the Teams product licence, with no feature-specific entitlement published.
claims.quote: You manage access to Teams at the user level by assigning or removing a Microsoft Teams product license. Except for joining Teams meetings anonymously, each user in your organization must have a Teams license before they can use Teams.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing
claims.claim: Teams Administrator is the documented role for using Teams admin center and managing these app controls.
claims.quote: To use Teams admin center, you must have a Teams Administrator role.

claims.claim: Some third-party Teams apps require a paid SaaS subscription.

claims.claim: App permission policies are deprecated for tenants using app-centric management.
